title: FlashDecoding++: Faster Large Language Model Inference with Asynchronization, Flat GEMM Optimization, and Heuristics
problem: LLM inference is bottlenecked by synchronization overhead between kernel operations and inefficient GEMM (general matrix multiplication) memory access patterns. Current decoding implementations use suboptimal scheduling that leaves hardware resources underutilized.
motivation: Reducing inference latency is critical for deploying large language models in latency-sensitive production systems where token generation speed directly impacts user experience.
method: The system avoids synchronization overhead by running operations asynchronously—letting them proceed without waiting for each other to complete. It optimizes matrix multiplication (GEMM) by improving the memory layout: instead of accessing memory in a scattered way that skips around (strided pattern), data is arranged to be read sequentially (contiguous layout), which improves cache efficiency and throughput. Heuristics then adaptively adjust the scheduling strategy and batch sizes based on the hardware and workload, preventing underutilization.
key_novelty: Combining asynchronous kernel execution with flat GEMM optimization to simultaneously reduce synchronization stalls and improve memory efficiency in token generation.
contributions: Asynchronous execution framework decoupling token-generation kernels to hide synchronization latency
Flat GEMM optimization eliminating strided memory access patterns in matrix multiplications
Heuristic-based adaptive scheduling that tunes execution strategy per batch and hardware
Measured speedup on GPU inference of large language models compared to baseline systems
limitations: Limitations not discussed; analysis limited to title.
primary_theme: asynchronous GPU kernel scheduling for faster LLM token generation
